exposure: Less Invasive Surfactant Administration (LISA) protocol incorporating intravenous fentanyl premedication and video laryngoscopy assistance
outcome: procedure-related adverse events (bradycardia, desaturation, arterial hypotension)
LISA failure (intubation with subsequent mechanical ventilation within 72 hours)
cohort: Preterm infants born at <32 weeks' gestation who received Less Invasive Surfactant Administration (LISA) according to a standardized protocol.
finding: The first-attempt success rate for LISA with fentanyl and video laryngoscopy was 62%, with attending physicians demonstrating significantly higher success than interns, and common periprocedural adverse events included desaturation (77%) and bradycardia (7%), while LISA failure occurred in 17% of infants.
